# Sources this skill cites

Each entry gives the exact quote relied on and the date it was checked. If a **Re-check by** date has passed, or the rule is an SBA rule, tell the user it may have changed and to confirm the current version (for SBA rules, the current SOP 50 10 and their lender).

## irs-form-8594-who-files

- **Source:** Instructions for Form 8594, Asset Acquisition Statement: purpose of form, Internal Revenue Service
- **URL:** https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8594
- **Supports:** In an asset purchase of a business, both buyer and seller report the sale on IRS Form 8594.
- **Quote:** "Both the seller and purchaser of a group of assets that makes up a trade or business must use Form 8594 to report such a sale if goodwill or going concern value attaches, or could attach, to such assets and if the purchaser's basis in the assets is determined only by the amount paid for the assets."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-earnouts

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: seller earnouts and buyer rebates, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** In a 7(a) change of ownership, seller earnouts are prohibited, while buyer rebates tied to business performance are allowed.
- **Quote:** "Seller earnouts/buyer rebates: Seller earnouts are prohibited; however, buyer rebates based on business performance are allowed because this is a benefit to the Borrower."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-lease-term

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 3: lease term when the borrower leases space, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Where this paragraph applies, the lender must get a copy of the lease, and for 7(a) loans the lease term including the borrower's renewal options should equal or exceed the loan term.
- **Quote:** "The SBA Lender must obtain a copy of the written lease between the Borrower and the landlord. For 7(a) loans, the lease term, including renewal options exercisable only by the Borrower, should equal or exceed the term of the loan."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-seller-consultant

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: seller may stay only as a consultant, up to 24 months, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** In an SBA 7(a) initial acquisition or business expansion, the seller can't stay as an officer, director, owner or employee, but the business may hire the seller as a consultant for up to 24 months in total.
- **Quote:** "Except as provided below, the seller in a Business Expansion or Initial Acquisition change of ownership transaction may not remain as an officer, director, stockholder, or employee of the business. If a transitional period is needed to assist the business, the small business may contract with the seller as a consultant for a period not to exceed 24 months (in aggregate, including any extensions)."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-seller-debt-equity

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: seller debt as equity, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Seller debt counts as equity for SBA purposes only if it is subordinated and on full standby, with no principal or interest payments for the life of the 7(a) loan.
- **Quote:** "Seller debt that is subordinated to the Lender and on full standby (no payments of principal or interest for the term of the 7(a) loan) may be considered as equity for SBA’s purposes."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26
